The heart of modern WordPress

The block editor, lovingly explained

Gutenberg turned a text box into a canvas. Everything is a block — and blocks compose into patterns, patterns into pages, pages into a whole site you can style without touching a stylesheet. Here's the joyful tour.

First principles

Everything is a block

A paragraph is a block. So is an image, a heading, a button, an embed, a table, a whole layout group. Each block is a small, self-contained unit with its own settings — and because they share a common model, they snap together predictably.

Press / anywhere and type a block name. Drag a handle to reorder. Select a few and group them. It feels less like wrestling a page builder and more like arranging ideas.

  • Content-first. Write naturally; structure follows your words.
  • Semantic output. Clean HTML that's great for SEO and accessibility.
  • Extensible. Developers can author custom blocks for anything.

<h2>A joyful headline</h2>
<!-- /wp:heading -->

HTML. Portable. Readable. Yours.</p>

Why blocks change everything

Four superpowers, no plugins required

Reusable & synced blocks

Build a call-to-action once, save it, and reuse it everywhere. Edit the original and every instance updates — perfect for footers, promos, and disclaimers across a big site.

Patterns

Whole pre-designed sections — hero, pricing table, testimonial wall — dropped in with a single click, then edited to taste. A library of patterns turns an empty page into a finished one in minutes.

Full-Site Editing

Headers, footers, archive templates, single-post layouts — all edited visually with the same block tools. The whole site becomes a canvas, not just the post body.

theme.json design system

One JSON file defines your palette, typography, spacing scale, and block defaults. It's a real design system — version-controlled, consistent, and editable in the UI through the Styles panel.

Design as data

Your whole look, in one file

theme.json is the quiet hero of modern WordPress. Define your colors, fonts, and spacing once, and every block inherits them. Change a value and the entire site re-themes instantly — in the editor and on the front end.

Here's a palette like one you'd declare. Click a swatch to copy its hex — design tokens you can actually hold.

{
  "version": 3,
  "settings": {
    "color": {
      "palette": [
        { "slug":"primary", "color":"#2c63ff" },
        { "slug":"grape",   "color":"#6d4aff" },
        { "slug":"coral",   "color":"#ff5d73" }
      ]
    },
    "typography": {
      "fontFamilies": [
        { "slug":"display",
          "fontFamily":"Fraunces, serif" }
      ]
    },
    "spacing": { "units":["px","rem","%"] }
  }
}

An honest comparison

Open WordPress vs. the walled gardens

We genuinely admire how polished hosted builders are. But here's where an open, self-owned WordPress site quietly pulls ahead over the long run.

Capability WordPress (open) Typical hosted builder Social platform
You own the content & dataFullyPartlyNo
Export & move freelyOne clickLimitedRare
Open-source & forkableYes (GPL)NoNo
Custom domain & SEO controlTotalGoodMinimal
Plugins & extensibility59,000+CuratedNone
Runs without a monthly feeYesNoFree*
Backward compatible for yearsSacredVariesChanges often
Choose your own hostAnywhereLockedLocked

*Free in price, but your audience and reach belong to the platform, not to you.

Blocks are the LEGO of the open web.

Snap, restyle, reuse, ship. Once it clicks, you'll never want to publish any other way.
